questions.prompt: A text says your bank account is locked and gives a link. What's the safest move?
options: Open your bank's official app or call the number on your card
questions.explanation: Use contact info you already trust, never the message's.

questions.prompt: Someone calls saying they're from your bank and asks for the code just texted to you. You should:
options: Hang up — never share one-time codes
Ask them to text it back
questions.explanation: A code you didn't request means someone is trying to get into your account.

questions.prompt: Which payment method is a big red flag?
options: A check to your utility company from your own bank
Paying your rent through the landlord's official portal
questions.explanation: Scammers demand gift cards, wires, crypto because they're hard to reverse.

questions.prompt: Your "grandson" calls in a panic needing bail money and says not to tell his parents. Best response?
options: Hang up and call him or his parents on a number you know; use your family code word
questions.explanation: AI voice cloning makes voices convincing; verify independently.

options: Your dog's name and birth year
questions.explanation: Long random-word passphrases beat short complex ones.

questions.prompt: Which account should get MFA first because it can reset your other accounts?
questions.explanation: Email is the key to password resets.

options: They fix security holes attackers already know about

questions.prompt: What protects you from a SIM-swap takeover of your phone number?
options: A port-out / account PIN with your mobile carrier and app-based MFA instead of SMS
questions.explanation: Carrier PINs and non-SMS MFA reduce SIM-swap risk.

questions.prompt: What does the 3-2-1 backup rule mean?
options: Back up every 3 days, 2 times, 1 week
questions.explanation: Multiple copies across media and locations.

questions.prompt: You sent money to a scammer by debit card an hour ago. First call?
options: Your bank, using the number on your card
questions.explanation: Speed matters; banks may stop or reverse payments.

questions.prompt: Freezing your credit at the three bureaus costs:
questions.explanation: Credit freezes and thaws are free.

questions.prompt: A teen is being threatened after sending a photo to someone online. What's the right first advice?
options: Stop replying, don't pay, save evidence, tell a trusted adult and report to NCMEC
Delete everything and tell no one
questions.explanation: Paying rarely ends it; reporting and support do.

questions.prompt: Which site gives a personalized identity theft recovery plan?
questions.explanation: The FTC's IdentityTheft.gov builds a recovery plan.
